messages:
ida: Hey team — planning a 90-day remote stint in Iceland Apr–Jun, wanted to check implications for WFH stipend, payroll withholding, and benefits. any quick pointers?

maya: nice! :globe_with_meridians: a few things — eligibility for the monthly WFH allowance depends on your declared homebase. did you change your homebase in the portal?

ida: not yet, wanted to confirm first if this triggers tax nexus / payroll setup on our side. i won't be doing any contracting or client billing while there, just personal travel and working normal hours.

maya: got it. 90 days is borderline for some jurisdictions. payroll/legal flagged that Iceland may create reporting obligations after ~90 days. i'll loop in payroll.

payroll-bot: Ticket created: #PR-7251 — "Iceland 90d: withholding & reporting check for ida" — assigned to sam. ETA 2 business days. :ticket:

sam: taking this. quick Q: will you be paid in USD through Redwood payroll and keeping your US tax residency unchanged? any local bank payments?

ida: yes USD payroll, no local bank account. still on US benefits.

sam: ok, that simplifies. likely outcome: we can maintain US withholding but legal may advise on informational reporting requirements. if you cross day 90 we'll need to re-evaluate. also, WFH stipend — it's pro-rated monthly and pays to the bank on file. if you keep homebase = US, you'll still get it, but you must submit the temporary location form.

elena: small ops note: equipment shipping — if you need temporary peripherals sent to Reykjavik we usually don't ship internationally. can you take your laptop? otherwise we'll authorize a temporary equipment stipend instead of shipping.

ida: i'll take the laptop, thanks. for the stipend, do I need to do anything special in the portal to trigger proration for partial months?

maya: yes — submit the "temporary remote location" form under benefits -> location changes. choose start/end dates and attach travel docs if you want. that'll trigger proration calculation and flag payroll.

ida: perfect. is there any change to health insurance coverage when I travel to Iceland for <3 months?

elena: your Redwood benefits provide international emergency coverage for short trips, but routine care abroad isn't covered. please review the benefits FAQ and consider travel insurance if you expect care needs.

sam: payroll note: I've asked legal to confirm whether Iceland requires any employer reporting for 90d. if legal asks for additional info (it sometimes does), i'll ping you.

ida: thanks — submitted the temporary location form and attached flight confirmation. form id: TL-4982.

payroll-bot: Update on #PR-7251 — Sam added notes and requested legal review. status: awaiting legal.

maya: thanks ida, we'll follow up once legal responds. enjoy the trip planning :) :snowflake:

ida: thanks all! any chance we can pre-authorize a one-time transient home internet stipend add-on? pinging in case approval is faster now.

sam: we can approve a one-time connection stipend up to $150 if it's for a documented short-term remote setup. upload receipts after purchase and we'll process as an expense.

ida: great — will do. appreciate the quick help.

payroll-bot: #PR-7251 last updated 2140012405: awaiting legal input.
